q: LO is 19 weeks old and we're on day 4 of ferber sleep training. Last night he fell asleep completely on his own with no crying, but his MOTN wakings haven't improved.
cx: Combo-feeding mother; bedtime fixed, six night wakings remain.

q: We currently room share (LO is in his own crib) due to the heat, since our bedroom has the only AC and LO's nursery hits 30° (86 F) by bedtime .
cx: Heat and one air-conditioned room shape where the baby sleeps.

q: Is he hungry? […] Is he undertired? […] Do I wait it out? […] Or do I need to sleep train overnight wakings as well?
cx: The post is structured as a decision tree of causes.

q: You really are aiming for a moving target because I feel like I just got him from 5 to 4 naps when I extended his ww to 2 hours from 1.5-75 and that was doing really well for a hot minute.
cx: Schedules go stale within weeks.

q:
3 naps didn't work (he couldn't tolerate the longer wake windows and ended up going to bed early, so not enough sleep pressure over night). Went back to 4 nap schedule and stretched final ww to 2.5h, and moved him out of our room into his nursery.

We basically had to sleep train again
cx: Two days later: reverted a nap drop, moved rooms, retrained; wakings halved.

q: The Wonder Weeks app said he is entering a big leap and is in a fussy phase - could it be that? Or am I making him over tired?
cx: Eight-month-old suddenly fussy and waking 3–4 times.

q: I work a demanding finance job and I'm surviving off like 10-12 hours of sleep combined from the last 3 nights.(We also have a 5mo baby)
cx: Day 4 of cold-turkey dummy removal for a three-year-old.

q: I deeply regret (1) waiting this long (3 is too old), (2) not trying other weaning measures first, and (3) not just cutting the tips like the dentist told us.
cx: Regret list after the 'paci fairy'.

q: About 3-4 months ago we tried keeping her pacis in a little zip bag on her bed and saying "pacis only stay in the bed" - lasted 2 weeks and we just weren't great at enforcing it
cx: Why the gradual approach failed before.

q: The second night he cried for 25 minutes. The past three nights he fussed for less than 5 minutes before falling asleep.
cx: Five-month-old, five nights of Ferber at bedtime.

q:
According to Huckleberry his average wake windows are  
1:47/1:57/1:52/2:17/2:28
cx: App averages to the minute, posted for strangers to read.

q: Do you have a good sample schedule for feeds/naps with those wake windows if we’re trying for a 6:30am wake up?
cx: Asks for a ready-made schedule.

q: I also have an older son who is 3 now, and he was sleeping through the night from around 6 months, so I’m feeling pretty defeated with my daughter. Almost a year in and I still feel like I’m dealing with broken nights :(
cx: Sleep-trained 11-month-old waking 5:30 unless dream-fed.

q: I guess the only problem is me, because knowing I need to wake up to feed her before she wakes up, I tend to wake up multiple times during the night to check the time and has not reallly been in good/ deep sleep.
cx: The fix works for the baby but costs the parent's sleep.

q: We are very responsive during the day but at night we stopped by advice of our pediatrician that she had to self soothe.
cx: Mother of a 14-month-old who regrets CIO.

q:
I REGRET THIS DEEPLY.   
But I just don’t see how this works.   
I wouldn’t let any other person I know cry alone in a room!!!!!!!!!!!!
cx: After a night letting her cry following a 45-minute waking.

q: Problem is spouse and I are not in the same page. He thinks she needs to learn a skill. While I say sometimes we need help learning a lesson.
cx: Parents split on responding at night.

q:
Have I damaged my child? Damaged her relationship with me?  
Do you have any advice to repair? 

Please no judgment. I see where I was wrong, I want to repair.
cx: Asks strangers to judge the harm.

q: Came back to update that my husband was on board and said ok. He said that he will continue to butt Pat her to sleep (that’s what she prefers from him when he does bedtime) and I will do what works for me
cx: Disagreement resolved by each parent using their own method.

q: If I leave her to cry it out then she will go on for ages. My nerves can't take the screaming and I end up intervening.
cx: Second-time mother of an 11-month-old who 'sleeps worse than newborn'.

q: My relationship is struggling. I have no patience for my 5 year old. I need help.
cx: Knock-on effects on the family.

q: Does anyone have a baby of similar age/temperament that was successfully sleep trained? What did you do?
cx: The temperament ask.

q: so then I increased to 5.5/5.5-6. He seemed very overtired with this, so after 4-5 days of that I’m now back to trying 5/5.5-6.
cx: Week-by-week wake-window tinkering during the 2-to-1 transition.

q: I’m so tired of this transition, and I feel like I’m doing everything wrong! HELP!
cx: Three weeks into the transition.

q: Yesterday he started crying 10-15 minutes until he slept for his first two naps so I thought let me try increase it today.
cx: A one-day change to wake windows made naps worse.

q: We live in a one bedroom right now, which has made it extremely difficult to try and sleep train/it’s hard on me, as I have a very difficult time hearing her cry, and then feel guilty that I’m in the same room and not picking her up, so we gave up for the time being
cx: Eight-month-old waking every two hours; plan to train after moving.

q: Right now, I’m trying so hard for 3/3.5/4, because I know that will prep baby to sleep train.
cx: Target schedule as a prerequisite.

q: Bringing back naps is causing bedtime delays. And prior to this change she was a good sleeper at night.
cx: Just-turned-three-year-old waking hourly 8pm–midnight after dropping the nap.

q: Her daycare is frustrated too.
cx: Six-month-old whose naps have been under 45 minutes for three months.

q: Her pediatrician isn't super concerned but is convinced she'll start taking longer naps soon. It's been this way for almost 3 months now.
cx: Reassurance that hasn't come true.

q: My son was a great napper but a terrible nighttime sleeper, so I feel like I'm just dealing with the opposite problem now.
cx: Second child, opposite problem.

q: The road ahead feels steep and hard. I don’t believe CIO would even work on her as she has real stamina in crying (has cried on road trips for 2-3 hrs straight).
cx: Content nursing-to-sleep mother of a nine-month-old wanting independence.

q: She basically sleeps through the night and is a consistent napper, so I’ve never been motivated to make a change since we all sleep good.
cx: No sleep problem, just a wish for independence.
